takeaways: Changing the setting of a control, like picking an option in a select, checking a box or choosing a radio button, does not automatically change context, unless people were told beforehand.
A change of context means a new page or window, a moved focus, or a major change to the page’s content that alters its meaning.
Keyboard users arrowing through a select can trigger every option on the way. A select that navigates on change throws them off on the first one.
Revealing a few related fields after a choice, just after the control, is usually fine. Pressing a button is activation, not changing a setting.
failures: A language select that reloads the page on change
A filter checkbox that jumps focus to the results
A form that submits when the last radio is picked
check: Use every select, checkbox, radio and toggle in the prototype. Does any of them navigate, submit or move focus?
For each one that does, check there is a visible message before the control that explains it.
Check filters that update results leave focus on the control.

quiz.question: A country selector in the footer reloads the site in the chosen region as soon as an option is picked. What is the best fix?
options: Add a loading spinner while the page reloads
Make the select larger so people pick carefully
Add a “Go” button that applies the choice
quiz.why: The change then happens on request. A spinner still changes context unannounced, and a larger select does not stop keyboard users from triggering options as they arrow through.

spec: For each form control, note what changes when its value changes.
Where a change of context is kept, write the advance notice and show it before the control.
Specify the apply button for selects and filters that navigate or reload.
review: What happens if someone arrows through this select one option at a time?
Does any control here act without a button press?
If this has to happen on change, where are people told first?
tradeoff: Instant filters and selects feel quick. Keep instant updates for content on the same page, keep focus where it was, and put navigation and submission behind a button.
system: Ship select and filter patterns in two documented modes: update in place, or apply with a button. Leave out a navigate-on-change mode.
pitch: Controls that act on their own surprise people and drive support calls. A button costs one click and removes the surprise.
